topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a microevolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous mutational processes and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogen risks and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore evidence linking environmental exposures to cancer risk through global epidemiological patterns and the debate over intrinsic versus extrinsic factors.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive malignant transformation, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a multi-factorial model.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and xenobiotic carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how radiation and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA damage and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, contextual susceptibility, and DNA damage mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic tumor promoters from initiators and assess how tissue development and host context modulate carcinogenic susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the analytical, epidemiological, and laboratory approaches used to detect carcinogen exposures and evaluate mutagenic potency.

topics.label: Conclusion and everyday risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic summarizes the lecture themes and concludes with the practical challenge of balancing carcinogenic risks against everyday benefits.
